current.text: Philadelphia acquired him from Boston in a trade for Paul George.
He is in the projected Philadelphia starting five with Tyrese Maxey, VJ Edgecombe, LeBron James and Joel Embiid.
His usage was a career-high 36% in Boston last season. Experts expect it to drop to about 27 to 30% because he now shares the ball with Maxey, Embiid and LeBron.
Experts say he is very unlikely to repeat 28.7 points per game. They expect his scoring to drop more than any other Sixers star's.
Even after the scoring cut, Josh projects him at about 25 points, 7 rebounds and 4 assists. He expects more rebounds and possibly better efficiency.
His minutes should stay high or go up under Nick Nurse, who plays his main players heavy minutes. He is projected for about 36 minutes.
His usage and minutes will move with the health of Embiid and LeBron. He may get a bigger role when they miss games.

He is expected to struggle more than LeBron to fit in at first. It is not clear whether he can play off the ball or as a spot-up shooter. The team is expected to have growing pains in October and November.

Experts expect him to slip from about 25th in category leagues last season to roughly the 35 to 45 range, a third or fourth round player. The newest call ranks him about 35 and says his rank of 44 is enough of a discount. Falling into the 60s would be too far.
He sold for 23 USD in an auction mock draft, which the expert called a good price. The expert hoped he would stay in the low 20s.
One expert calls an ESPN ADP of 20 far too high.
The Sixers have 13 back-to-backs this season, and 3 of them fall in the fantasy playoffs.
Philadelphia is projected to win about 51 to 52 games. Experts also expect the team to manage the stars' workloads.

durable.text: Scoring is his main fantasy value, and points are his strongest category.
His turnovers are a clear weakness, well below the player pool and his position.
Besides points, he gives modest help in rebounds, assists, steals and threes. His FG% and FT% are not ideal but do not hurt a team much.
Experts say nine-cat rankings underrate what he gives in head-to-head category leagues.
He is worth more in points leagues than in category leagues. Last season he ranked about 10th in points leagues and about 25th in category leagues.
The experts disagree about his defense. Josh calls it a little overrated, and Mark calls him a more than solid defender.

note: Brown went for 29 USD in our league last season. The prices now point lower: Yahoo values him at 23 USD (average cost 24.2), and ESPN values him at only 7 USD (average cost 18.8), so the 23 USD he sold for in the latest mock is a fair target. He fits punt TO builds best, because his 2.9 projected turnovers are his only flagged weakness and his 24 points are a clear strength. Early in the season, check his usage and shot share next to Maxey, Embiid and LeBron, and whether Nurse really plays him about 36 minutes.
